edges.description: Hypothalamic hamartoma formation disrupts pituitary signaling, leading to endocrine insufficiency including adrenal insufficiency.
Failure of normal ventral hypothalamic development yields the non-neoplastic hamartoma that is the cardinal feature of the syndrome.
Disrupted anterior-posterior patterning of the limb bud produces the postaxial or mesoaxial extra digits of this syndrome.
Loss of normal hypothalamic input to the pituitary produces a spectrum of anterior pituitary hormone deficiency.
ACTH deficiency within that pituitary insufficiency causes secondary adrenal insufficiency, the potentially lethal neonatal complication.
The hamartoma is itself the seizure generator: its interneuron-like neurons fire spontaneously, so the gelastic seizures arise within the lesion rather than in cortex.
Ectopic GnRH secretion by the hamartoma activates the gonadal axis ahead of time, producing central precocious puberty.
